title: Newborn screening (heel prick test)
what: A few drops of blood are taken from your baby's heel onto a special card. The test checks for rare inborn conditions that need treatment right away.
why: For all newborns, usually in the maternity hospital on day 2 to 5 of life. In premature babies, it may be later.
duration: a few minutes; results usually come in 1 to 3 weeks
tell_doctor: If your baby was born early or had a blood transfusion
If your baby is on special feeding or IV drips
Your exact address and phone number, so you can be contacted if a repeat test is needed

prepare.title: Feeding
prepare.text: The test is usually done a few hours after a feed. The nurse will tell you the time.

prepare.title: Warmth
prepare.text: Warm feet give blood faster. Put socks on your baby.

prepare.title: Stay close
prepare.text: You can hold your baby or stay nearby. Ask the nurse.

bring: Your baby's and your documents, if the test is not in the maternity hospital
The referral, if it is a repeat test
steps: Your baby's foot is warmed and wiped
The heel is pricked with a tiny lancet
Drops of blood are placed on circles on a paper card
A cotton pad is pressed on the spot
The card is dried and sent to the lab
feel: Your baby may cry. The prick is quick
Breastfeeding, a pacifier, or a cuddle right after helps calm your baby
after: The small mark on the heel heals in a few days
If all is well, usually no one calls
If a repeat test is needed, you will get a call. It does not always mean illness

faq.q: I got a call asking for a repeat test. Is that bad?
faq.a: Not necessarily. Often it is because there was too little blood on the card or the test was done too early. Repeat it as soon as you can.

faq.q: Which conditions does this test check for?
faq.a: Several rare inborn conditions of metabolism and hormones. If they are treated early, the child grows up healthy.

reminders.text: Your baby's heel prick test is soon. Put socks on so the feet stay warm.
